A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same EDITLORD research, with readable text, equations, tables, figures and complete Appendices A–E. The appendices match apart from pagination; no material gaps prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original code-editing experiments across three tasks, including baseline comparisons, ablations, robustness, length generalization and human-guided editing (Tables 1–4).

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results and appendix analyses, with a revised baseline value in Table 1.

M1.justification: The ADD/MERGE/PRUNE rule-discovery algorithm, functional specifications, rule-conditioned training and inference, and Appendix D's two-step rule matching are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use HQ for performance optimization, AnghaBench/HumanEval-Decompile for decompilation, and SVEN/CWEval for security hardening. Robustness transformations and longer-code test coverage are also retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same Prompt, CoT and task-specific Finetuned baselines. Comparator membership in the other experiments is unchanged; the added related-work citations do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Reported splits, model sizes, metrics, training budgets, sampling settings, robustness procedures and length thresholds are unchanged. The updated CodeSage citation does not document a changed encoder or evaluation metric.

E4.justification: Component ablations, robustness and length-generalization tests, human-guidance experiments, rule-frequency analyses and Appendix C cases are retained (Tables 2–5). Figure 1 redraws the same illustrative code comparison.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Tables retain the same point-estimate and comparison-delta reporting practices.

E6.justification: Under unchanged reported settings, Table 1 changes DeepSeek-Coder 6.7B Prompt Correct@1 for performance optimization from 6.0% to 60.0%. EDITLORD remains at 36.0%, reversing this comparison. Figure 1 also removes its 2× and 5× speedup annotations; other result-table values are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical problem formulation, probability factorizations, rule-set operations and metric definitions are unchanged. Neither version adds or removes theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and headline claims about editing performance, functional correctness, robustness, generalization and applicability across editing modes.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 extends the existing correctness caveat to acknowledge that DeepSeek-Coder 6.7B prompting also outperforms EDITLORD on functional correctness in performance optimization. Section 4's execution-feedback limitations and lack of correctness guarantees remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Hardware disclosures and Appendices A, D and E retain identical prompts, rule-learning details and hyperparameters, including batch size, learning rate, epochs and inference temperature. No code or data access information changes.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds citations to editing research including CODIT, InstructCoder, GRACE and Can It Edit?. Section 3.1 replaces the CodeSage citation to Li et al. (2023) with Zhang et al. (2024). The substantive positioning of EDITLORD remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Small wording, hyphenation and figure-terminology edits accompany the expanded results sentence. The narrative organization, section sequence and appendix structure are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn with revised panels, highlighting and rule checklists. Table 1 updates best-score bolding, and added references cause pagination changes. The remaining displays and appendix layouts are retained.

improvement.justification: The revised Table 1 comparison receives an explicit qualification in Section 3.2, improving reporting of a baseline advantage. Updated CodeSage attribution and broader editing citations improve scholarly context. Figure 1 loses quantitative speedup labels, a limited tradeoff; the method, experimental scope and appendix evidence otherwise remain unchanged.
